fact: UNFPA Tunisia reports three training workshops on 20 November, 4 December and 11 December 2025, organised by the Ministry of the Interior and the National Institute of Health with the statistics institute and the Centre National d'Informatique and UNFPA support, involving 72 municipalities in all and giving civil status officers and heads of municipal districts intensive training on the Medania digital system for accurate and prompt declarations; the total number of municipalities is not given.

The Tunisia country report, citing UNFPA 2021, describes the Civil Register, the MADANIA system, as a digitised civil registration system and centralised database managing the civil status records of all Tunisian nationals and of foreigners with registered civil status, covering births and deaths as well as marriages and divorces (no date given for the statement; the document's published date is used).

fact: The Tunisia country report, citing UNFPA 2021, states that the births and deaths held in the MADANIA civil register come under the authority of the Ministry of Interior, and marriages and divorces under the Ministry of Justice (no date given for the statement; the document's published date is used).

fact: The Centre National de l'Informatique's page states that the national civil status system Madania manages all civil status documents, naming birth, marriage, divorce and death, publishes them at municipalities, municipal districts and commercial sites, and builds a centralised database (the page is undated; the document's published date, a proxy year, is used).

The World Bank diagnostic states that civil registration is conducted by local governments and centralised in the Madania database run by the Ministry of Local Affairs and the Environment (MALE), with the National Informatics Center (CNI) responsible for its technical implementation; the report says its contents are current as of September 2019.

fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that MALE, the technology ministry (MTCEN) and CNI have developed a strategy to upgrade Madania, including a move to a paperless system and linked birth, marriage and death records, with the new system to be developed over 2020 and deployed during 2021; contents current as of September 2019.

fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that data on births, deaths and marriages are entered into Madania by local officials, and cites MALE (2019) for 18.53 million birth acts, 4.14 million death acts and 3.8 million marriage acts recorded as of 2018.

fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that civil events are recorded at municipal level in physical ledgers and then manually entered into Madania by local officials, in a hierarchical local, regional and central database synchronised in nightly batches; contents current as of September 2019.

fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that as of 2015 Madania, first deployed in the municipality of Tunis in 1992 and rolled out nationally from 2004, was accessible from nearly 481 sites (all municipalities plus regional and commercial sites) and 1,300 workstations, used by about 1,500 people; it gives 264 municipalities before 2016 and does not say how many offices register in it.
